faqs.question: What does the Fungal Culture and Identification test - Other Sample measure?
faqs.answer: This test detects the presence of fungal infection in your body.

faqs.question: Why is the Fungal Culture and Identification test - Other Sample done?
faqs.answer: • To diagnose fungal infections and determine the appropriate antifungal treatment. • To identify the specific type of fungi causing the infection and select the most effective antifungal medications.

faqs.question: When is the Fungal Culture and Identification test - Other Sample recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: This test is recommended if you have symptoms of a fungal infection, such as persistent itching, redness, or discharge from the vaginal area or other sites prone to fungal infections. It is also useful for patients with compromised immune systems, patients with recurrent infections, or those who have been exposed to sources of fungal contamination.

faqs.question: What if the results of the Fungal Culture and Identification test - Other Sample are abnormal?
faqs.answer: If the results show positive growth of fungi, it indicates a fungal infection.

faqs.question: What to expect during the Fungal Culture and Identification test - Other Sample?
faqs.answer: During the test, a sample of vaginal swab or discharge will be collected using a sterile, leak-proof container. The sample will be sent to the laboratory for testing through the MALDITOF (Vitek MS) technology.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the Fungal Culture and Identification test - Other Sample?
faqs.answer: • Follow any additional instructions provided by your doctor or the testing facility. • Inform your doctor if you have any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with Fungal Culture and Identification test - Other Sample?
faqs.answer: • KOH Examination: A microscopic examination of a sample to detect fungal elements directly • PCR (Polymerase chain reaction) Testing: A molecular technique that detects fungal DNA (Deoxyribonucleic acid) to help identify specific types of fungi • Antifungal Susceptibility Testing: Determines which antifungal medications are most effective against the identified fungus

faqs.question: What is the Fungal Culture and Identification test - Other Sample also known as?
faqs.answer: Fungal culture with MALDITOF or Fungal identification by Vitek MS

faqs.question: What is a fungal infection?
faqs.answer: A fungal infection is caused by the overgrowth of fungi in or on your body. Fungi are microorganisms that can thrive in warm, moist environments. Common fungal infections include vaginal yeast infections, athlete's foot, and ringworm.
